_why: STAGE 2 IMPLEMENTATION against the design pinned by the #2061 spike and its lifecycle ADDENDUM (.agents/tasks/2061-analysis.md on branch fix/2061-fable, commits 820ac26d3 + a46319aaa). FR-106 Phase 4 (#275, PR #280) landed PlanNode::Subquery and a ~90-arm consumer cascade and was marked complete; the PRODUCER never landed, so nothing constructs the variant and ColumnResolution — #1749's binder — cannot see inside a subquery. THE KEY INSIGHT, from the addendum: post-#1966 binding is NOT an optimizer rule. build_plan_inner runs producer -> propagate_schemas -> bind_plan (fallible, pre-optimizer, plan/mod.rs:398) -> optimizer; decorrelation runs later still, on the AST (primed_query.rs:609). The side table's host key is dereferenced EXACTLY ONCE, inside bind_plan. So keys are live only within [producer -> propagate -> bind] and DEAD BY CONTRACT afterwards. That dissolves the lifecycle problem that ten spec-review rounds surfaced as five symptoms (pushdown eliminating hosts, CSE merging entries, decorrelation swapping inner queries, propagation skipping entries, the strict gate rejecting valid correlations): NO RULE runs while the keys are live, so no rule needs to maintain them. Entries are bind-time 'as written' metadata, not an executable mirror — the main plan tree also describes the pre-decorrelation query and never needed fixing either. PINNED PLACEMENT: a side table on the LogicalPlan root wrapper, subquery_plans: Vec<SubqueryPlanEntry> keyed by host PlanNodeId, with Expr::Subquery COMPLETELY UNTOUCHED so the runtime is preserved by construction. Rejected and re-verified: enclosing-node fields break 188 full-struct-literal sites across 55 files; Expr carrying Arc<LogicalPlan> breaks Expr's PartialEq derive, which CSE relies on (cse.rs:832-838). Subqueries EXECUTE correctly today — 300 non-Kafka subquery tests pass — this adds plan-level visibility only.

anchors._note: the root wrapper gaining `subquery_plans`. `pub fn new` appears twice in this file — LogicalPlan::new MUST default the new field. That single fact is what keeps this an ~11-file change instead of a 46-file one.

THE PRODUCER site. The only point where schema_source is in hand — the inner plan's Scan schemas need it, and lifting later (e.g. as an optimizer rule) would build blind inner plans and reproduce today's silent pass.

the binder. Its arm at :757 recurses with ctx.reset() and leaves correlation_columns UNTOUCHED, violating logical.rs:1192-1193. Fixed here by consuming entries at the host node, where both the inner scope and the outer schema are in hand.

blast_radius._note: 122 refs / 49 files measured EXACTLY as velo-dispatch measures it (`git grep -F -o ... -- src tests examples`, dispatch line 326). A line-count method returns 120 because two matches share a line; 122 is the number the gate checks. NOT the edit surface — the spike established that as ~11 files (7 src, ~4 test).

tests._note: fail_to_pass names indicative; NEITHER test exists — write them, run against e4c3511c4, and RECORD THE FAILURE OUTPUT before implementing. The reject test is the capability that does not exist today. Its ACCEPT TWIN is equally required: two-scope resolution must not reject a VALID correlated subquery, including a JOIN-ON one — a false rejection is worse than the gap this closes. Also required: one LIFECYCLE test driving a pushdown-eliminated host and CSE-mergeable subqueries through the FULL pipeline, asserting bind diagnostics and EXPLAIN are unaffected. pass_to_stay are nextest FILTER EXPRESSIONS. FLOOR: `test(/subquery/) and not test(/kafka/)` was 300 on the spike host — capture your own.

acceptance: read .agents/tasks/2061-analysis.md on branch fix/2061-fable IN FULL, including the lifecycle addendum (commit a46319aaa) which AMENDS §3. Where the addendum and the original §3 disagree, the addendum wins

SubqueryPlanEntry { host: PlanNodeId, ordinal: usize, plan: Arc<LogicalPlan> } and subquery_plans on the LogicalPlan root wrapper. LogicalPlan::new defaults it — LogicalPlan has ZERO full struct literals across src and tests (343 uses of ::new), verified, so this cascades to nothing

PRODUCER in PlanBuilder::from_ast_with_schemas — where PlanNode::Subquery is finally CONSTRUCTED, as the ROOT NODE of each entry's plan. Walk the built tree for Expr::Subquery in its OWN nodes; build each inner plan via from_ast_with_schemas (NOT build_node, which returns a bare PlanNode with no wrapper); map SubqueryType -> SubqueryKind; extract correlation_columns by walking the inner WHERE for outer-scope references; push an entry keyed by the host node's PlanNodeId. The producer PROPAGATES each inner plan at construction (builder.rs:804 sets the precedent) — schema_propagation.rs is NOT touched

SubqueryType -> SubqueryKind mapping states how AnyAll gets its operator. SubqueryType carries NO comparison operator (ast.rs:1195-1212) while SubqueryKind::AnyAll requires one (logical.rs:59-78) — the walker must take it from the ENCLOSING binary expression. Specify that extraction, or exclude ANY/ALL from lifting in this pass and say so explicitly; do not leave it to be improvised

OWNERSHIP: each wrapper owns only its own nodes' subqueries. Do not descend into embedded LogicalPlans that survive in the tree — CreateStream.as_select (:312), CreateTable.as_select (:320), Insert.values (:329), Union.left (:413), Union.right (:414); each carries its own table. StreamSource::Subquery (:804) is OUT of scope — its wrapper is discarded, only the schema survives, so a table there would be unreachable

LIFECYCLE, MADE MECHANICAL rather than promised: `host: Option<PlanNodeId>`, and bind_plan CLEARS it to None after consuming it and asserting the bijection. A post-bind dereference then cannot compile into a silent wrong answer — it sees None. Entries themselves survive for EXPLAIN 'as written'; only the key dies. This replaces a doc-comment contract, which the review correctly noted is not verifiable from a diff, with a state change that is

BIND-TIME CONSUMPTION in plan/mod.rs's bind_plan: resolve each entry's interior against the inner scope, then resolve correlation_columns against the HOST node's input schema — TWO-SCOPE resolution, not an exclusion list. Only a name resolvable in NEITHER scope rejects. For a JOIN host the outer scope is the merged left++right schema, the same one the binder already uses for ON conditions (column_resolution.rs:621-640). RECURSIVE: bind_plan currently makes ONE ColumnResolution.rewrite pass over the root and has no side-table traversal, so entries on EMBEDDED wrappers — Union.left/right, CreateStream/CreateTable.as_select, Insert.values — would be produced and never bound. Consume each child wrapper's table too, with a per-wrapper bijection. Requires a NESTED-WRAPPER test (a subquery inside a UNION branch and inside a CTAS)
column_resolution.rs:757's contract violation fixed: it currently recurses with ctx.reset() and leaves correlation_columns untouched, contrary to logical.rs:1192-1193

an END-OF-BIND BIJECTION ASSERT: every entry's host resolves to a live node, and every Expr::Subquery reachable in the tree has exactly one entry. Asserted where the keys are still live, so it is a theorem about the producer rather than a hope about every rule

EXPLAIN renders entries under an explicit AS WRITTEN (BIND-TIME) heading — they describe the query as written, not what executes after decorrelation. Use the ANNOTATED path: format_annotated's invariant is that its traversal and StreamExecutionEngine::collect_annotations visit the same nodes in the same order (explain.rs:108-133); update both, and exercise real EXPLAIN output
